title: Meeting Rooms III
summary: Given an integer n, there are n rooms numbered from 0 to n-1.
statement: Given an integer n, there are n rooms numbered from 0 to n-1. A 2D integer array meetings is provided where each meeting is defined by a start and end time. Each meeting is allocated to the room with the lowest number that is currently unused. If no room is available, the meeting is delayed to the next available time slot with the same duration. When a room becomes free, the meeting with the earliest original start time is given the room. The task is to return the room number that hosted the most meetings, with ties broken by the lowest room number.
constraints: Rooms are numbered 0 through room_count-1 and meeting start times are unique.
Use the lowest-numbered idle room; if none is idle, delay the meeting to the earliest room while preserving its duration.
Return the room with the most meetings, breaking count ties by the lowest room number.
hints: Scheduling needs one ordering for free times and another for idle room numbers.
Keep idle room numbers and busy (finish,room) pairs in separate min-heaps.
Release rooms by start time, assign the smallest idle room or delay onto the earliest busy room, then increment that room count.
Heap ordering enforces every tie rule directly; processing unique starts in sorted order also preserves the required priority among delayed meetings.
editorial: Heap ordering enforces every tie rule directly; processing unique starts in sorted order also preserves the required priority among delayed meetings.

tests.explanation: Both rooms host two meetings after delays, so the lower room number zero wins the tie.
Rooms one and two each host two meetings, and room one is the smaller tied index.
